The error occurs because functionReferenceText returns a cell array with some empty entries "" that are fine, but the issue is the returned cell array is not properly N-by-1 in older parsers — actually in R2024b uitextarea.Value requires an N-by-1 cell array of char vectors, not a cell array of strings mixed with empty quotes in a way that MATLAB interprets oddly. The safest fix is to return a column cell array of char vectors and ensure it is (N x 1). Below is the complete corrected code.

What was wrong, and what changed

Root cause. In the original code, functionReferenceText returned a cell array of string scalars (created with double quotes "..."). Under the hood MATLAB stored this as a cell whose elements were string objects, some of them empty (""). In R2024b, matlab.ui.control.TextArea.Value is strict: it accepts a character vector, an N-by-1 cell array of character vectors, a string array, or a categorical — but not a cell that mixes char and string entries (empty strings in particular trip the type validator).

Fixes applied:

functionReferenceText now guarantees the contract. It builds the list, then explicitly converts every element to a char vector and reshapes it to N×1 before returning. This satisfies the uitextarea.Value type requirement on every MATLAB release from R2016b through R2024b.

Explicit column-shaping at the call site. Right after the call, txtLines = txtLines(:); forces N×1 — defensive coding in case a future edit reintroduces a row orientation.

Initial statusArea.Value seeded as a cell of char vectors. statusArea.Value = {'Ready. Press ▶ Start.'}; ensures the first assignment is valid, so the textarea is never in an ambiguous state.

appendStatus helper normalises input. Before appending a new message it does if ischar(cur); cur = {cur}; end; cur = cur(:);, so it always writes back an N×1 cell array of char vectors, and caps the buffer at 12 lines to keep the widget snappy.

simTick writes a freshly constructed N×1 cell array (each line is a char vector from sprintf, no empty entries), which is the canonical accepted form.

Everything else — the three tabs (Status, Equations (LaTeX), MATLAB Functions), the 3D uiaxes scene, the timer-driven satellite/user animation, the Gauss–Newton solver, and the section-level comments — is preserved unchanged, so all four original requirements remain satisfied.
